newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end lower on Fed inaction.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end lower on Fed inaction.

text.p: The Swedish debt market ended mixed on Wednesday with rates at the short end a little higher after the National Debt Office T-bill auction.
The issue was oversubscribed in the three and twelve month maturities but underscribed for six month paper for which bills worth 2.2 billion crowns were issued and the average rate was 3.89 percent.
Immediately after the acution the six month T-bill rate rose one basis point to that level.
A favourable inflation report released by the central bank on Tuesday continued to push down longer yields.
The Fed's decision to keep rates unchanged also helped to drive yields down.
The ten-year bond yield fell eight basis points to 6.79 percent. The spread between German and Swedish long yields narrowed by six basis points to a very low 91.
The crown gained to 4.4030 to the mark from 4.4120 Tuesday.
"There is a balance on both the buying and the selling side. The range is narrow and we don't see any external impacts", one dealer said.
Thursday's focus will be U.S. statistics.
